thought.text: The goose wrapper downloads from GitHub (reachable). Now let me start the infrastructure containers (postgres, redis) with the environment:

reasoning_content:
goosew.sh downloads goose from GitHub Releases — an external resource, but GitHub is probably reachable (I was able to download nodejs.org without any issues). The version is pinned in `packages/data/goose.config.json`.

Next, let me start the infrastructure: postgres + redis with the environment variables.

action.command: cd /workspace && cat packages/data/goose.config.json; SVA_ENABLE_MONITORING=false POSTGRES_PASSWORD=sva_local_dev_password APP_DB_USER=sva_app APP_DB_PASSWORD=sva_app_local_dev_password REDIS_PASSWORD=sva-secure-password-2026 WASTE_DATABASE_PROVISIONER_PASSWORD=sva_waste_provisioner_local_dev timeout 400 docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.override.yaml up -d --scale app=0 2>&1 | tail -12; echo "EXIT: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "cd /workspace && cat packages/data/goose.config.json; SVA_ENABLE_MONITORING=false POSTGRES_PASSWORD=sva_local_dev_password APP_DB_USER=sva_app APP_DB_PASSWORD=sva_app_local_dev_password REDIS_PASSWORD=sva-secure-password-2026 WASTE_DATABASE_PROVISIONER_PASSWORD=sva_waste_provisioner_local_dev timeout 400 docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.override.yaml up -d --scale app=0 2>&1 | tail -12; echo \"EXIT: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}\"", "security_risk": "MEDIUM", "summary": "Start postgres and redis containers"}
